argument: Both challengers dispute the conviction and the sequencing, not the thesis — and both are right on the process points. Concessions first, defense second. (1) Staleness: confirmed against my own feed this round — the pair-ratio endpoint still serves the 2026-07-28 print (2.0274), and the valuations endpoint remains 429 rate-limited with news still empty. I cannot independently re-strike percentile/z-score from my tools. However, macro_asia_japan's fresh print (NFLX 74.12 / RSPC 36.40 = 2.036, Aug 7 close) is verification, not just critique: the ratio has moved +0.4% in 11 days, so the dislocation the trade is built on is intact at execution-relevant levels. I accept the amendment as a condition: percentile/z-score/technical signals re-struck on current prints at execution, and if the ratio has drifted materially above ~2.10 the risk/reward must be recomputed before entry. (2) Stop vs. vol: the math is correct and I accept it. NFLX 90d σ 2.21% vs RSPC 1.00% implies pair residual σ of roughly 1.9–2.4%/day depending on correlation; a 7.3% stop distance is ~3–4 daily σ of the ratio, not the comfortable buffer my framing implied. Defense of the level itself: 1.8835 is the 52-week ratio low — a structural thesis-break level, which is where a stop belongs in this framework (the stop exists to kill a wrong thesis, and a break of the year low IS the thesis being wrong). The correct fix is sizing, not stop placement: this should enter at the low end of the band with the risk budget assuming elevated stop-out probability. I also add the yen-carry unwind tail to the risk list — it is exactly the wrong macro regime for this trade archetype if it fires, and it wasn't in my original list. (3) CPI sequencing: macro_ceemea's strongest point, and I adopt it as a formal amendment — entry is conditional on the 2026-08-12 CPI print clearing with the ratio holding above 1.8835. A hot print that gaps NFLX through the ratio low resolves the question for free; entering before a binary macro event with zero fundamental confirmation was poor sequencing and I've amended the catalyst window accordingly (entry post-CPI, proof points still the Oct print). (4) Regime: partially accepted. EEM/ACWI RS -7.5% describes a selective DM-led tape where washed-out names stay washed out — but the RSPC hedge is precisely the instrument that neutralizes that regime exposure; the residual is NFLX idiosyncratic plus US growth beta, which I own knowingly. What survives the challenges: the dislocation is real and challenger-verified (deepest relative dislocation in coverage; ~2.03–2.04 on a fresh print, still bottom-decile of the 52-week range); the momentum turn evidence stands on the scan (KST bullish crossover, MACD histogram +0.356 rising, OBV rising against the price low, +6.9% 1W vs XLC +2.8%); the reward/risk at re-struck levels is still ~2.9:1 to the 38.2% retracement; and neither challenger identified any fundamental falsification — the bear case remains 'it can stay cheap,' which is a timing argument, answered by the CPI-conditional entry and reduced size. Net: two independent seats argued this is a 4-5 on process grounds, and the staleness concession plus the CPI sequencing amendment are material enough that I revise honestly rather than hold. Conviction to 5 — the setup is intact and verified, the entry conditions are now properly specified, but it remains a technical-led counter-trend trade with zero fundamental confirmation, sized small, entered only after the macro print.
